Question: What is your review of the Avengers 4: Endgame teaser trailer (December 2018)?
Answer: The traile… oops! The teaser gave a glimpse (a really short one) of the movie, but with hidden messages, which most comic fanatics might have noticed. Endgame references from Avengers: Infinity war And Avengers: Age of Ultron This brief moment in Age of Ultron isn’t just important to Endgame simply because it drops the title. It’s important because the moment as a whole is there to remind the Avengers why they’re there. Not just to protect the people of Earth from themselves, but to protect them from even greater threats, that Tony has seen up-close and personal, that could destroy their entire world. Tony lost in space This much-anticipated trailer starts with a shot of Iron Man's helmet, badly broken in the wake of his last fight with Thanos. He's seemingly all alone on a spaceship, without power, floating along. He's recording a message to Pepper Potts on his helmet, adding in a little humor. This could be immediately following the end of Infinity War, which would imply that Nebula (Karen Gillan) is potentially on the same ship. This is Nebula’s hand which, I assume, is touching Tony's shoulder. Thanos scarecrow Thanos is briefly shown tilling the fields on his quiet farm, basking in the glory of having just murdered half of all life in the universe. And as he does so, the trailer features a shot of his old armor, now propped up as a bizarre sort of scarecrow. This scene draws inspiration directly from the 1991's comics Infinity Gauntlet Thanos is actually shown retiring from villainy and tilling the fields on a remote alien world. In that story, Thanos is retreating in disgrace more than gloating over a hard-won victory. As in the movie, Thanos acquires the full Infinity Gauntlet in this story and uses it to wipe out half of all life in the universe. The difference is that he quickly loses the Gauntlet due to his own hubris and has his work quickly undone. Thanos realizes that deep down, he always wanted to lose. Faced with his own psychological weakness, Thanos retires to live a quiet, simple life. He even uses his costume as a scarecrow just as he does in this movie. Ronin Jeremy Renner suited up in black and gold, weilding a weird katana-esque blade on the streets of a rainy Japanese city. Ronin was an identity that Clint Barton used, instead of Hawkeye, from about 2007 to 2010 in Marvel Comics. Why the name, costume and weapons change? Well, in 2004, Clint died. Then, in 2007, he was brought back to life. While he was dead, the world had necessarily moved on. A young avenger named Kate Bishop was calling herself Hawkeye — and wearing a purple costume and using trick arrows — and Clint thought she was doing pretty well with the name. Wishing additionally to hide his return from the wider world for a bit, he borrowed a code name, costume and weapons from a fallen Avenger, Maya Lopez, to become Ronin. In Avengers: Endgame, he may have darker motivations. For all we knew, in Infinity War, Clint Barton had retired from the superhero game. A tie in comic and the movie itself confirmed that he’d taken a plea deal after breaking the Sokovia Accords in Captain America: Civil War, and returned home to his family's farm. What could have dragged him away from his wife and kids? “We lost, all of us,” Captain America says in the Endgame trailer. But he says “we lost family” just as the trailer cuts to Clint in Japan, moodily wiping his blade on one arm. Did Clint Barton’s family survive the snap? Odds are not looking so good. Scott Lang Avengers: Endgame’s trailer sets up a surprising reveal: the surviving Avengers presumed that Scott Lang, aka Ant-Man, was killed when Thanos wiped out half of the universe’s life, only to have him turn up on their doorstep at the end of the trailer. A post-credits scene from Ant-Man and the Wasp explains that while other people on Earth were shattering into dust following Thanos’ snap, Ant-Man was in the quantum realm. Ant-Man may not have been killed by Thanos’ snap — officially referred to as the Decimation, according to Marvel Comics — possibly because he wasn’t within the universe at the time. While Lang is exploring the quantum realm, he’s warned to look out for time vortexes, whose name implies that if he passes through, could reconfigure time itself. This means when Lang teams up with the Avengers — or the remaining Avengers — they could use those time vortexes to reverse time and save the population from devastation. How Scott gets out of the quantum realm is a mystery. Now, the issue with Avengers trailers — or any movie trailer — is you can’t trust them. Remember that the Hulk starred in Avengers: Infinity War’s trailers and then never appeared in the actual film. This could just be a cool gesture to throw fans from guessing what’s going to happen — like we are — but this does help to explain how the Avengers could possibly defeat Thanos going forward. Did I love the trailer? Absolutely!!! Question: What is the difference between a programmer and a developer?
Answer: A programmer is someone who would spend most or all of his time in front of his system coding. They are responsible for writing, testing, debugging/troubleshooting and maintaining the source code of computer programs. A programmer is like a cook in a restaurant. On the other hand, a software developer is more like a professional chef. Not only can they cook to a high standard, but they can take a more creative and conceptual approach to what they’re making. This means finding out what their target market wants, creating a plan for how to make it, and coming up with a series of instructions that they can give to other cooks. Chefs do this for restaurants and software developers do this for programmers. Programmers are all about code. It is their job to take the specifications given to them by a developer and turn them into a functioning application. To do this they put the developer’s ideas into a language that the computer can understand and follow. Software developers can be thought of as project managers who can code while programmers are technicians. When comparing a programmer and a developer, a developer should be able to code but their main job is finding ways to solve problems. To do this, they need to figure out what those problems are and then figure out the technical framework for solving them.

Question: What is your favorite movie scene that gives you goosebumps every time you watch it?

They both discuss the definition of power. Goeth: You are never drunk. You know that’s… that’s a little control. Control is power. That’s… power. Schindler: Is that why they fear us? Goeth: We have the fucking power to kill, that's why they fear us. Schindler: They fear us because we have the power to kill arbitrarily. A man commits a crime, he should know better. We have him killed, and we feel pretty good about it. Or we kill him ourselves and we feel even better. That's not power though. That's justice. It's different than power. Power is when we have every justification to kill, and we don't. Goeth: You think that's power? Schindler: That's what the emperors had. A man stole something, he's brought in before the emperor, he throws himself down on the ground, he begs for mercy. He knows he's going to die. And the emperor pardons him. This worthless man, he lets him go. Goeth believes that fear drives power. The way Schindler tries manipulating Goeth by attacking the problem at it’s core is remarkable. The second scene is where Schindler leaves his factory for good as the war is over and he is sure to be hunted as a member of the Nazi party. Schindler: I could have got more out. I could have got more. I don't know. If I'd just... I could have got more. Stern: Oskar, there are eleven hundred people who are alive because of you. Look at them. Schindler: If I'd made more money... I threw away so much money. You have no idea. If I'd just... Stern: There will be generations because of what you did. Schindler: I didn't do enough! Stern: You did so much. Schindler: This car. Goeth would have bought this car. Why did I keep the car? Ten people right there. Ten people. Ten more people. Schindler: This pin. Two people. This is gold. Two more people. He would have given me two for it, at least one. One more person. A person, Stern. For this. Schindler: I could have gotten one more person... and I didn't! And I... Question: What is your biggest mistake or regret?
Answer: Buying this notebook from U.S via a friend. A $1100 HP Spectre X360 Notebook. $1100 which I withdrew from my provident fund account. I was so excited the day my friend landed. Little did I know that the excitement will be short lived. Our strategies didn’t go as planned and the laptop got caught in customs (my friend was carrying his own laptop too, unknowingly). They gave me a brand new Macbook Pro. Major facepalm! Now I forced myself to use my notebook on weekends to justify the cost I paid for it. One fine night after binge watching a TV series, I kept my notebook on my desk on charging mode, next to my water bottle. Next day I woke up only to realise that the bottle was lying on the floor, empty. The notebook was drenched with a chemical compound consisting of 2 atoms of Hydrogen and 1 atom of oxygen, otherwise called water. I disconnected the notebook immediately, wiped it clean and kept it in a rice bag for 3 days. Called a technician who, after inspection, inferred “It’s too late. The motherboard is fried”. These words were more deadlier than “I think we should break up”. The price for a new motherboard was INR 26,000. Buying this expensive notebook was my worst investment which I regret till date. Question: What made you quit your job?
Answer: After 2 years and 2 months of working in a product based organization (Zycus Infotech, Mumbai) as a Software developer and learning lots of new tech, I left the company as work had become monotous. Joined an MNC (Oracle Financial Services and Software), with a decent hike and hopes of working on new tech. First month @OFSS: My local desktop was setup with few softwares in the first week. Client side desktop, which we connect to via VPN was partially setup at the end of first month. Basically, I had no work for this month, no softwares to learn new things (installing development related softwares in local machine was prohibited). Used online compilers for the same. Even that was blocked after few days :(. Imagine, Stack Overflow - Where Developers Learn, Share, & Build Careers was blocked in my ODC. Second month @OFSS: Remote desktop was fully setup with roles and permissions to servers and tools and work was allocated with no bar on deadline. Realized I was allocated to the project as a Support engineer (was totally disappointed). I was in my comfort zone, doing work with speed of a snail. Came in late and left early as manager was onsite and there was no one senior to track the ins and the outs. Eventually, had to join companies free services (gym, indoor games and sleeping area) to kill time. Third month @OFSS: Work had become monotonous which mostly involved solving existing bugs and other support level activities. Continued my extracurricular activities like going to gym, playing TT and carom, cricket and badminton, sleeping in sleeping area for an hour, etc. Fourth month @OFSS: By now, my weekdays went as follows: Oh, and did I mention I also went to watch movies between 12pm to 3pm? :P Fifth month @OFSS: Well, I had become good at playing carom and TT, and looked fit by now. But wait! Had I learnt anything related to my profession in these past 4 months? Did I develop something incredible that I can put in my resume? NO! Actually, I was forgetting the techs I learnt in my 2 years of exp. This is the moment I realized I have to stop being in my comfort zone. Tried analyzing which project I could switch to to enhance my skills, but found nothing. Most projects were using outdated techs, rest had no vacancy. Decided to learn by self and build my resume. Sixth month @OFSS: Still worked with the speed of snail, but learnt new techs at the speed light (well obviously not with the speed of light :p) and built my own projects in my spare time. Built a strong resume and posted it on job portals. Started giving interviews. Rejected many due to less hike (no one was meeting my expectations as I was leaving my current organization within 6 months). Also was rejected by a few. Learnt from rejections and gave more interviews! Currently, I am working with a product based startup. Services they offer are not much compared to MNC's but the work is awesome with lots of new techs, which requires continuous learning. Salary they offered was what I had asked for. FYI, now I just spend 30 min tops on extra-curriculars as deadlines have bars now. :) Life begins at the end of your comfort zone - Neale Donald Walsch

Question: What is the difference between Quora and Facebook?
Answer: Quora is a question-and-answer networking site where people ask, edit and answer questions. Facebook is a huge social networking site which generates revenue mostly on adverts and billions of mindless users. Quora connects you with people you wish you knew. Facebook connects you with people you wish you didn't. Quora is a place with people smarter than you. Facebook is a place with people happier than you. Quora users are curious about ideas. Facebook users are curious about other users. Quora made me like people I never met. Facebook made me hate people I knew. Quora develops you. Facebook develops from you.
